sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Crochan, also known as Cruacha, stands among the heroines and goddesses of Irish story. While pregnant, she served Etain, the Tara queen who ran away from her realm. Crochan delivered Medb, later a celebrated queen and goddess, inside a Connacht cavern. People used several names for that cavern. Some knew it as Oweynagat, others as the Cave of the Cats. A further title was the mound of a fairy called Sinech, known as Sid Sinche. Sinech was an obscure being whose name referred to large breasts. From outside the cavern seemed a plain opening in the ground. Crochan, however, beheld it as a splendid fairy dwelling. She kept living there after her daughter built a hilltop fort that she named Cruachan to honor her. The word Crochan itself signified a vessel. At times she bore the double name Crochan Crocderg, meaning the blood-red cup.

okr.objective: Crochan is the servant who gave birth to the queen Medb in a Connacht cave.
